name: Obsidian
tagline: Connect your ideas through linked notes stored in Markdown files you control.
description:
Obsidian is a local-first note-taking and knowledge-management app built around Markdown files in a folder you control. It lets you write ordinary notes, link them together, search across the collection, and shape the workspace with plugins, themes, and views instead of locking information into a proprietary document format.

The central idea is that notes become more useful when connections are easy to create and revisit. A project brief can link to meeting notes, research, people, tasks, and source material, while backlinks and graph views reveal where a topic already appears elsewhere in the vault.

## Features

- Store notes as local Markdown files in a vault you can inspect, back up, and use with other tools.
- Create internal links, backlinks, tags, embeds, and graph views to connect related ideas across a growing note library.
- Search across note content and properties, then use folders, templates, and metadata to organize a preferred workflow.
- Extend the app with community plugins, themes, automation, and specialized views when the core editor is not enough.
- Use Obsidian across macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android, with optional sync and publishing services available separately.
- Keep a simple writing practice if desired, without requiring every note to participate in a complex system.

## Where it fits

Obsidian is best for people who want long-lived notes in files they control and enjoy linking information over time. It is particularly strong for research, writing, personal knowledge management, and project documentation.

It is not the quickest choice for disposable notes or people who want a fully designed workflow out of the box. Sync, collaboration, and plugin choices also need deliberate setup if they are important to your work.

## Privacy and requirements

Obsidian stores vaults as local Markdown files and does not require an account for the core app. Optional Obsidian Sync, Publish, third-party sync tools, community plugins, and web services each change that boundary. Community plugins execute code with the user's permissions, so install them selectively and keep an independent backup of important vaults.

Obsidian includes a free tier. Sync from $4/month, billed annually.
